cross_language_rules.description: Protect intentional English names inside non-English text
cross_language_rules.rule: If a Latin-script span is Title Case, known entity, acronym, product/game/software name, username, URL, code token, version, model number, or user-defined protected phrase, replace it with a placeholder before translation and restore it afterwards.
Detect http://, https://, www., domain names with paths/query strings, invite links, and deep links; preserve the full span byte-for-byte unless URL normalization is explicitly requested.

cross_language_rules.description: Preserve Discord mentions and channel references
cross_language_rules.rule: Protect <@id>, <@!id>, <@&id>, <#id>, @username, role mentions, and channel-style references before translation.

Keep emoji code points, skin-tone modifiers, variation selectors, flags, keycaps, and ZWJ sequences unchanged and in the same relative position unless target-language punctuation requires harmless spacing.
Protect <:name:id> and <a:name:id> as atomic tokens; do not translate the emoji name inside the token.

cross_language_rules.description: Preserve platform timestamps and time markup
cross_language_rules.rule: Protect Discord timestamps such as <t:unix>, <t:unix:R>, ISO timestamps, and explicit machine-readable date-time tokens; translate only surrounding prose.

cross_language_rules.description: Do not translate fenced code blocks
cross_language_rules.rule: Protect triple-backtick fenced blocks including language tags. Translate code comments only if explicitly requested.
Protect text inside single-backtick inline code spans as exact code tokens.
Protect Windows paths, POSIX paths, Android paths, UNC paths, filenames with extensions, and URI-like resource paths; do not translate path segments.
Protect shell commands, executable names, flags beginning with - or --, environment variable assignments, package coordinates, and command arguments that are syntactic tokens.
Protect patterns such as v1.2.3, 1.2.3-beta, build 26200.9168, OS3.0.301.0.WNCMIXM, kernel versions, commit hashes, and release tags.
Protect alphanumeric model names such as RTX 5090, RX 9070 XT, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Xiaomi 14, SM-S928B, 23127PN0CG, and similar product identifiers.

cross_language_rules.description: Preserve usernames, handles, and gamer tags
cross_language_rules.rule: Protect @handles, platform usernames, discriminator-style names, mixed-case gamer tags, and user-defined names unless the user explicitly asks for transliteration.
Protect the # marker and named hashtag token. If the hashtag is a natural-language campaign phrase, optionally provide a translated gloss separately but do not replace the original tag by default.

cross_language_rules.description: Do not expand or translate established platform/gaming acronyms blindly
cross_language_rules.rule: Keep tokens such as GG, AFK, OP, FPS, DPS, PvP, PvE, NPC, CPU, GPU, RAM, API and SDK unchanged unless the target community convention strongly localizes them.

If an entry has can_generate=false and can_recognize=true, normalize its meaning for translation but do not emit that slang form in the target output unless the user explicitly requests that exact style or the surrounding conversation already uses it.
Do not generate region-marked slang outside its region unless the user requests that dialect. Recognition may remain enabled globally.

cross_language_rules.description: Translate profanity by pragmatic function rather than literal anatomy
cross_language_rules.rule: Classify profanity as reaction, intensifier, insult, doom statement, sexual/literal meaning, or filler before selecting a target equivalent. Prefer natural force and intent over dictionary literalness.

Inside a non-English sentence, preserve Latin-script package names, mod names, libraries, repo names, branch names, commit IDs, game item names, and exact UI labels when they appear intentional rather than ordinary foreign-language prose.
